questions.question: When you need something from someone, you typically:

options.text: Ask directly and clearly for what you need
Demand it and get frustrated if they don't comply immediately
Hint at what you need and hope they figure it out
Act nice but make subtle jabs if they don't give you what you want

questions.question: When someone criticizes you, you usually:

options.text: Listen calmly and consider if the feedback is valid
Get defensive and criticize them back
Apologize immediately even if you don't think you're wrong
Say it's fine but hold a grudge

questions.question: In a disagreement, you tend to:

options.text: Express your viewpoint while respecting theirs
Argue forcefully until they see your point
Go along with what they want to avoid conflict
Agree outwardly but sabotage or complain behind their back
Clearly state your limits while being respectful
Set harsh boundaries and don't care how others feel
Have trouble saying no even when uncomfortable
Say yes but then don't follow through

assertive.title: Assertive Communication
assertive.description: You have an assertive communication style. You express your needs and opinions clearly while respecting others. This is generally the healthiest communication style.
traits: Clear and direct expression of needs
Respects both your rights and others' rights
tips: Continue to model this healthy communication for others
Maintain this balance even in stressful situations

aggressive.title: Aggressive Communication
aggressive.description: You tend toward aggressive communication. You express your needs forcefully, sometimes at the expense of others' feelings and rights.
traits: Focused on winning rather than understanding
tips: Take a breath before responding when upset

passive.title: Passive Communication
passive.description: You have a passive communication style. You may avoid expressing your needs or opinions to prevent conflict or please others.
traits: Puts others' needs before your own
tips: Remember that your needs are valid
Start with low-stakes situations to build confidence

passive_aggressive.title: Passive-Aggressive Communication
passive_aggressive.description: You show passive-aggressive tendencies. You may avoid direct confrontation but express negative feelings indirectly through subtle actions or words.
traits: Indirect expression of anger or frustration
May use sarcasm or backhanded compliments
May procrastinate or 'forget' to avoid conflict
tips: Identify and acknowledge your true feelings
